ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: In this course, students learn how to interpret critically the literature, film, and media produced within and about the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, from its establishment in 1948 to the present day. The course will focus on questions of revolution and democracy, the Stalinist political formation and Soviet Occupation, and on the ways that literature and visual culture create and recreate "North Korea" as a fantasy space. This class is offered via video-conference and is hosted by the University of Minnesota. The class meets Sept. 3 - Dec. 11, 2013, with finals following after the last day of instruction. The course will meet in 4057 Lincoln Hall.
